subject: FinSecure RFP: detailed support coverage & incident communication
messages:

Subject: RFP: support coverage & incident communications (FinSecure)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier this week. As part of our RFP appendix we need a written response to a few operational questions so our security and procurement teams can sign off. Attached is the Support Appendix PDF with the sections we need filled in - items 2, 3 and 5 are highest priority for us.

Specifically, please confirm the following in detail:
- TAM coverage model (hours, contract SLA vs. TAM responsibilities)
- On-call rotation: number of engineers, escalation windows, after-hours support and holidays
- Incident severity definitions and P1/P2 target response and resolution times, including follow-up cadence and post-incident RCA policy
- Communication channels used for incident notifications and real-time collaboration (phone, PagerDuty, Slack, Zoom) and expected notify windows
- Evidence we can include in our audit: incident logs, audit trail retention, SOC2 artifacts access process

Can you provide a written response and any supporting playbooks or templates by COB Wednesday (Aug 2)? I attached the appendix as a reference.

Appreciate it,
Anna

Subject: Re: RFP: support coverage & incident communications (FinSecure)

Hi Anna,

Thanks for the appendix. Please find an initial response attached: 'Redwood_TAM_Coverage_20260830.pdf' — it covers our TAM engagement model, hours, and handoff processes. High-level summary below:

- TAM coverage: standard TAM for Enterprise includes business-hour coverage (Mon-Fri, 9am-6pm local) and optional 24x7 on-call for P1s as an add-on.
- On-call: our 24x7 on-call uses a 7-day rotation for the primary on-call engineer plus a secondary responder; escalation after 15 minutes (pager -> phone -> exec alert).
- Incident targets (default): P1 initial response <= 15 mins, P2 initial response <= 1 hour. Resolution SLAs are workload-dependent; we provide estimated MTTR targets per model/throughput in the attached spreadsheet.
- Notifications: we integrate with PagerDuty and can publish to a customer-managed Slack channel; Zoom bridge available on request.
- Audit materials: SOC2 report available under NDA; incident logs and audit trail exports can be provided for the contract term + 90 days by default, extended retention options available.

Next steps: Marcus will follow up with a proposed incident comms playbook and a draft SLA matrix for you to review. Would you be able to confirm whether FinSecure requires 24x7 P1 coverage as a must-have or preferred?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Anna Simpson <anna.simpson@finsecure.com>

Date: 2026-08-31T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: support coverage & incident communications (FinSecure)

Evelyn,

Thanks — the summary helps. A few clarifying items from security and procurement: could you expand on the following?
1) For the 24x7 on-call: please confirm average time-to-engage (time until engineer starts work, not just acknowledges) and whether you provide a named escalation contact at the account exec level.
2) Does Redwood support customer-managed Slack channels with message retention locked down to our workspace? We need evidence the channel cannot be accessed by non-FinSecure parties.
3) For incident logs: format and delivery mechanism (S3 export, API access, or CSV email).
4) Are there any planned maintenance blackout windows and how are those communicated?

Also, FinSecure requires that critical incidents (P1) trigger an immediate exec-level notification within 30 mins if the incident is impacting production availability for customers. Can you confirm you can meet that and include the escalation path (names/roles acceptable)?

If acceptable, we'll schedule a 30-minute technical runthrough with Derek and one of your TAMs to validate the details.

Thanks,
Anna

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T11:50:00-07:00
Subject: FW: FinSecure clarifications — proposed SLA matrix and escalation path

Evelyn/Laura,

Following Anna's notes, I've put together a short SLA table and an incident escalation path we can share. Attached are 'Incident_Comms_Playbook_v1.docx' and 'Redwood_SLA_Table_20260901.xlsx'. Key points:

- Engage vs acknowledge: our on-call engineers acknowledge PagerDuty within 5 minutes on average; time-to-engage (start triage) target is 15 minutes for P1s. We commit to a named escalation contact at manager level for every enterprise TAM.
- Slack: we support customer-managed Slack channels. Access is controlled by the customer workspace; our agents join via guest accounts and do not retain admin rights. We will sign a channel access addendum for the contract.
- Incident logs delivery: standard export options are S3 bucket export (preferred), API access for pull, or scheduled CSV exports. We can ship logs daily for the incident window and provide a consolidated archive post-incident.
- Blackout windows: routine maintenance windows are proposed Sundays 0200-0400 PT; critical security patches may require urgent maintenance with 72-hour notice where possible. All planned maintenance is communicated via the customer portal and via email 7 days prior.
- Exec notify: commit to exec-level ping within 30 minutes for P1s. Internal escalation path (roles): Primary on-call -> On-call manager -> TAM manager -> SVP of Customer Ops. We will provide named contacts on contract signature.

Notes: we should ask for confirmation on S3 vs API for log handoff and whether FinSecure requires FIPS endpoints.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Support Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: Incident_Comms_Playbook_v1.docx; Redwood_SLA_Table_20260901.xlsx

- We support customer-managed Slack channels; we'll sign an addendum to confirm guest access restrictions for your workspace.

- Exec notification for P1 within 30 mins guaranteed; escalation path will be included in the final playbook.
- Maintenance windows: standard Sunday 0200-0400 PT; urgent security windows with 72-hour notice where feasible.
